source: E. K. Anderson et al. (ALPHA Collaboration), 'Observation of the effect of gravity on the motion of antimatter', Nature 621, 716-722 (2023), doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06527-1, Table 1 'Results of the release trials'. Open access, CC BY 4.0.
transcribed_from: Europe PMC full-text XML of PMC10533407 (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC10533407/fullTextXML), table-wrap Tab1
notes: Events are escapes in the 10-20 s window of the 20 s mirror ramp-down, inside the z-cut regions [-32.8,-12.8] cm (down) and [12.8,32.8] cm (up).
All values are corrected for the expected cosmic-ray background (hence fractional and occasionally negative counts).
They are NOT corrected for the relative detector efficiency of the up and down regions; the paper's P_dn in its Fig. 5 comes from a likelihood analysis that does apply that correction.
Bias labels are nominal (programmed) values in units of g; the paper's Fig. 5 plots derived biases that differ slightly.
Positive bias encourages antihydrogen to exit at the bottom. The +/-10 g rows are calibration trials.
